title: Impact of environmental parameters on marathon running performance
authors: El Helou N, Tafflet M, Berthelot G, Tolaini J, Marc A, Guillaume M, Hausswirth C, Toussaint JF
population: All finishers of six major marathons (Paris, London, Berlin, Boston, Chicago, New York), 2001-2010, 60 races; temperature, humidity, dew point, sea-level pressure and NO2/SO2/O3/PM10 gathered per race
findings: Performance distributions per race-year were normal, with mean and SD varying with environmental factors.
Air temperature and performance were significantly correlated through a quadratic model, so there is an optimum temperature rather than a monotonic effect.
The optimal temperature for maximal mean speed depends on performance level; above the optimum, speed decreases and withdrawal rates increase.
Ozone also affected performance but its effect might be linked to temperature; the other environmental parameters (humidity, dew point, pressure, other pollutants) had no significant impact.
Conclusion: air temperature has the major influence of all climatic parameters on marathon running.
limitations: Race-level aggregates, not individual runners; correlational; no solar or wind data; city-level weather; humidity effect may be masked by collinearity with temperature; the abstract does not give the optimum temperature values or the direction of the shift with ability.
implications: Model temperature as a U-shaped (quadratic) penalty around an optimum. The ability-dependent optimum is not quantified in the abstract, so keep it a tunable parameter calibrated from Ely 2007 and Mantzios 2022.
Do not add a separate humidity or pressure term on top of temperature or WBGT; no independent effect was found (humidity is already inside WBGT).
Treat high-ozone days as a possible small extra penalty (low confidence); no number is justified.
Include a withdrawal-risk warning that rises with temperature above the optimum.

verification.notes: Crossref (PLoS ONE, 2012-05-23, El Helou) and Europe PMC abstract (PMID 22649525) re-fetched. All findings stated. Rewrote the garbled first implication. Full text not read, so optimum values are not quoted.
